result.topic: PAN-OS XML API type=op "request license info" — exact request/response XML shape

confirmedFacts.claim: The official Palo Alto SDK's PanDevice.op(cmd, cmd_xml=True) (default) converts a plain-text op command into XML via panos.string_to_xml(), which tokenizes the string on whitespace and builds a strictly nested element chain in word order (first word = outermost tag). For 'request license info' (3 unquoted tokens) this produces request > license > info, with 'info' having no text/children so it serializes as an empty element. Net request XML: <request><license><info/></license></request> (self-closing vs <info></info> are byte-different but XML-semantically identical empty elements).
confirmedFacts.evidence: def string_to_xml(value, quote='"'): tokens = value.strip().split(); ... elm = ET.Element(token); ... root.append(elm) / graft_point.append(elm); ... return ET.tostring(root, encoding='utf-8')  [lines ~407-470]

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-os-python's PanDevice.request_license_info() literally calls self.op('request license info') (cmd_xml defaults True) then parses the ElementTree result with result.findall('./result/licenses/entry'). This confirms the response path is ./result/licenses/entry relative to the <response> root element (i.e. <response status=...><result><licenses><entry>...</entry></licenses></result></response>).
confirmedFacts.evidence: def request_license_info(self): ... result = self.op("request license info"); return self._format_result_as_license_list(result)  /  for x in result.findall("./result/licenses/entry"): ans.append(License(...))  [lines ~5354-5440]

confirmedFacts.claim: Each <entry> under licenses has exactly these child tags in the official SDK's parsing (all accessed with x.find('./TAG').text, i.e. all are simple non-attribute text leaf elements): feature, description, serial, issued, expires, expired, authcode. 'expired' contains the literal string 'yes' or 'no' (compared with == "yes"), not a native boolean. 'issued'/'expires' contain date strings like 'March 24, 2017', or the literal string 'Never' for a non-expiring license (issued/expires are parsed with a '%B %d, %Y' format, falling back to raw text on parse failure).
confirmedFacts.evidence: License = collections.namedtuple('License', ['feature','description','serial','issued','expires','expired','authcode']) ... if value is None or value.text is None or value.text == "Never": return None ... date_format = "%B %d, %Y"

confirmedFacts.claim: The community SDK pan-python (kevinsteves) documents a real captured example against a live PAN-OS VM-50 device: running `panxapi.py -t vm-50 -Xjro 'request license info'` (which converts the same text command to XML via an equivalent word-nesting algorithm and prints only the <result> content as JSON) returned: {"licenses": {"entry": [{"authcode": null, "description": "Standard VM-50", "expired": false, "expires": "Never", "feature": "PA-VM", "issued": "March 24, 2017", "serial": "015351000001360"}]}}. This independently corroborates both the licenses/entry container name and all 7 child field names against an actual device response, not just SDK-side assumptions.

pan-python's own text-to-XML converter (pan.xapi.PanXapi.cmd_xml, used by panxapi.py's -X flag in the example above) implements the identical word-nesting algorithm independently of pan-os-python's string_to_xml, and for 'request license info' traces out to the same nesting order request > license > info with 'info' left childless/textless -- cross-validating the request body derivation from two independently-written SDKs.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def cmd_xml(self, cmd): def _cmd_xml(args, obj): ... obj.append('<%s>' % arg); _cmd_xml(args, obj); obj.append('</%s>' % arg) ... args = cmd.split(); _cmd_xml(args, obj); xml = ''.join(obj)  [lines ~557-586]

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's PanConfig.__serialize_py (the routine that turns the raw XML ElementTree into the JSON/dict shown in the panlicapi.rst example) hard-codes 'entry' and 'member' tags to always be serialized as a JSON list even when only one sibling exists, and converts a childless/textless element to null (None), a childless element whose text is exactly 'yes'/'no' to boolean true/false, and any other childless element's text to a plain string. This explains why the captured JSON example shows expired:false and authcode:null, and confirms the underlying live-device XML literally contains <expired>no</expired> and an empty <authcode/> (or <authcode></authcode>) element -- i.e. authcode is present as an empty tag even when a license has no auth code, not omitted.
confirmedFacts.evidence: _tags_forcelist = set(['entry', 'member']) ... if not len(elem) and not text_strip and not attrs: obj[tag] = None; return ... if text_strip == 'yes': obj[tag] = True elif text_strip == 'no': obj[tag] = False else: obj[tag] = text  [lines ~24, 149-207]

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's XML response envelope parsing (used by both -j/-p output and general status handling) confirms the root element is <response> carrying a status attribute (defaulting to 'success' if absent, otherwise the literal value e.g. 'error'), and that <result> is a direct child of that root -- matching the project's existing pan_base.py `_xml_request` (`root.get('status')`) and pan_firewall.py's `root.findall('./result/licenses/entry')` usage where `root` is the parsed `<response>` element.
confirmedFacts.evidence: self.element_root = element; self.element_result = self.element_root.find('result') ... if 'status' in response_attrib: self.status = response_attrib['status'] else: self.status = 'success'  [lines ~285-317]; query['type'] = 'op'; query['cmd'] = cmd  [__type_op, lines ~930-943]

confirmedFacts.claim: Official docs.paloaltonetworks.com (the 'PAN-OS XML API Request Types and Actions' page) and pan.dev's XML API index page do NOT publish the literal request/response XML for 'request license info' anywhere -- confirming the existing pan_api_research.md's stated gap is real: Palo Alto's own documented method to obtain this string is `debug cli on` on a live box. Neither page was found to contradict anything derived from the SDK source above; they simply don't cover this specific op command with a worked example.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Page describes type=op generically ('operational mode commands, including checking system status and validating configurations') with no license-specific example or generic op-command XML sample.

confirmedFacts.claim: The underlying CLI text output of 'request license info' (found via a general web search, not directly re-verified against docs.paloaltonetworks.com in this pass) uses field labels Feature, Description, Serial, Issued, Expires, Expired? -- lowercase-and-no-punctuation forms of which match the XML/JSON tag names confirmed above 1:1 (feature, description, serial, issued, expires, expired). This is corroborating but was not fetched from a primary URL I could directly verify content of, so it is rated lower confidence than the SDK-source findings.
confirmedFacts.evidence: Search-engine-summarized CLI transcript: 'Feature: WildFire License / Description: ... / Serial: ... / Issued: January 13, 2020 / Expires: March 08, 2023 / Expired?: no / Base license: PA-VM'

confirmedFacts.claim: Palo Alto's official LIVEcommunity forum (community.paloaltonetworks.com / live.paloaltonetworks.com) has multiple threads specifically about fetching license info via the XML API (e.g. thread IDs 322968 and 250748) that likely contain real captured request/response XML from members, but their content could not be directly retrieved in this research pass: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on both thread URLs, and the sandboxed browser tool's site policy blocked navigation to live.paloaltonetworks.com entirely. Only a web-search engine's AI-generated summary of those pages was available, which is not treated as a verified primary source here (though it stated a request form of `/api/?type=op&cmd=<request><license><info></info></license></request>`, which happens to match the SDK-derived structure above, i.e. it is consistent but not independently confirmed by me from the raw page).
confirmedFacts.evidence: WebFetch result: 'The server returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.' Browser navigate result: 'https://live.paloaltonetworks.com is blocked by policy.'

remainingGaps: No official docs.paloaltonetworks.com or pan.dev page was found publishing the literal request-license-info XML verbatim (Palo Alto's own documented way to get it is `debug cli on` on a live box). This gap, already flagged in pan_api_research.md, remains open on the 'official first-party' front even though it is now well-covered by SDK source-code evidence.

The LIVEcommunity forum threads that plausibly contain real member-captured request/response XML (thread 322968 'Request license fetch thru API call on all pan devices', thread 250748 'How do I use API support to pull active license report from Panorama?') could not be read in this pass -- WebFetch got HTTP 403 and the sandboxed browser blocked live.paloaltonetworks.com by policy. If the orchestrator has authenticated/allowed access to that domain, re-fetching those two threads directly (not via a search-engine summary) would be the last missing corroboration layer.

Nothing in the SDK source clarifies whether a firewall with ZERO installed licenses (e.g. a brand-new/base-only unit) returns an empty <licenses></licenses> element, omits <licenses> entirely, or returns something else -- the forcelist/None-serialization rules only cover the 'at least one entry' case seen in the captured example. Suncoast's fleet almost certainly has licenses installed, so this is a low-priority edge case, not a blocker.

Not verified in this pass: exact behavior of the `target=<serial>` parameter combined specifically with 'request license info' when the connector is pointed at Panorama (i.e., does Panorama proxy this specific op command to the named firewall and return that firewall's licenses, or Panorama's own?). pan_api_research.md already confirms target= works generically for type=op; this pass did not find a license-specific worked example of that combination.

Whether the DNS Security subscription line's exact 'feature' string is confirmed remains an open gap from the original research pass -- this pass did not find a new source resolving it, and it wasn't in scope of this specific research task.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: No fix needed for correctness -- the existing request body `"<request><license><info/></license></request>"` and response xpath `"./result/licenses/entry"` in get_license_info() are now CONFIRMED correct (high confidence) by two independent SDKs (official pan-os-python and community pan-python), cross-validated against a real captured device response. Recommend updating the method's docstring to remove the 'NOT CONFIRMED' language for the request body and xpath, and instead cite this research's sources (github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python panos/base.py and panos/__init__.py; github.com/kevinsteves/pan-python doc/panlicapi.rst).

Add an `authcode` field to the parsed dict in get_license_info() (currently only feature, description, serial, issued, expires, expired are extracted). Official SDK's License namedtuple and the community SDK's captured JSON example both show `authcode` as a 7th child tag on every <entry> (empty/None when a license was applied without an auth code, e.g. the built-in PA-VM base license). Add: entry.findtext("authcode") to the dict being appended, mirroring the other five findtext() calls at lines ~79-84 of the current file.

Optional robustness note (not a bug): the confirmed XML has `<expired>yes</expired>` or `<expired>no</expired>` as literal text, not a native boolean -- current code's `entry.findtext("expired")` correctly returns that raw string as-is, so no change is required there, but any downstream consumer of this dict must compare the value against the string 'yes'/'no' (as pan-os-python does: `.text == "yes"`), not treat it as a Python bool.

Move item #1 in the 'Items That Must Be Confirmed Against a Live Suncoast Firewall Before Production Use' list (exact XML request body for request license info) from open-gap to confirmed, citing github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python and github.com/kevinsteves/pan-python source code as the evidence basis (source-code-derived confirmation via a real captured device example, in lieu of an official docs.paloaltonetworks.com page or direct access to Suncoast's own device).
